_comment: Two policies with different jobs. COLOUR is pre-existing debt being swept page by page, so it reports as a warning: the count should fall every time anyone touches a stylesheet, but it does not block. TYPE and BREAKPOINTS are enforced as errors, because they are clean as of the phase 01/02 work and must stay that way. `npm run lint:css` therefore exits 0 today and can gate CI — a new hard-coded font size or a 23rd breakpoint is what breaks the build.

color-no-hex.message: No hand-typed colours. Use a token from app/styles/tokens.css.

declaration-property-value-allowed-list.message: Use a --fs-* token from app/styles/tokens.css, not a literal size. See docs/design-system.md.

media-feature-name-value-allowed-list.message: Only four breakpoints exist: 380px (narrow phone), 599px (phone), 820px (tablet), 1180px (narrow desktop), min-821px (desktop). See docs/design-system.md.

declaration-property-value-disallowed-li.message: This value exactly matches a --sp-* spacing token -- use var(--sp-1, --sp-1-5, --sp-2, --sp-2-5, --sp-3, --sp-3-5, --sp-4, --sp-4-5, --sp-5, --sp-5-5, or --sp-6) from app/styles/tokens.css instead of the literal. See docs/design-system.md.

overrides._comment: tokens.css is where the palette is DEFINED, so literals are correct here and nowhere else. Permanent.

THE EXEMPTION LIST for the type rule -- migration debt, not a design decision. This array may only ever get shorter: as each page is migrated out of globals.css, delete its entry. When it is empty, the migration is finished. Never add to it.

elo-guide/guide.css is a DELIBERATE, PERMANENT exception, not migration debt -- do not read this as a shrinking-list entry. It's a self-contained marketing/explainer page with its own intentional type scale (Barlow Condensed display faces, a .7rem-1.2rem body range, heavy clamp() use) that predates and deliberately doesn't match the app's 8-role --fs-* scale. Forcing it onto --fs-* would fight the page's own editorial design rather than fix an inconsistency -- see docs/design-system.md's "Where this stands" section for the reasoning. If this page ever gets its own dedicated token set, that's a separate design decision to make explicitly, not a mechanical migration.
